# Public package transport repair

The original public package cache included local environment links that Python's safe tar extraction rejects. One archive also included an installed reference environment. This repair removes those unmanifested artifacts so the packages work with the benchmark's existing fetch command.

| Item | Count |
|---|---:|
| Public instance packages | 88 |
| Repacked archives | 18 |
| Archives copied byte-for-byte | 70 |
| Removed environment symlinks | 189 |
| Removed environment files | 21538 |
| Removed environment directories | 1591 |
| Frozen file hashes verified after safe extraction | 16762 |
| Original archive bytes | 6,691,614,720 |
| Release archive bytes | 5,742,141,440 |

Only unmanifested symlinks and the `private/refenv` environment tree are eligible for removal. The repair stops if an eligible entry or any of its descendants appears in a frozen manifest. All retained file bytes, the frozen manifests, task inputs, graders, references, and controls are preserved. Unmanifested validation outputs and obsolete Core working files are retained to keep the repair narrow.

Only `package_sha256` and `package_bytes` change in the instance catalogue. Every `manifest_sha256` remains unchanged. This changes distribution archives, not task definitions or recorded scores.

## Reproduce and verify

```bash
python tools/repair_release_packages.py ORIGINAL_CACHE RELEASE_DIRECTORY
```

The script checks each source archive against its registered hash or the original hash recorded above, builds deterministic replacement archives, extracts all packages with `tarfile`'s `data` filter, and verifies every frozen file before updating package hashes and sizes. Existing cached originals can be reused after the catalogue update because their original hashes remain in the repair record.
